findings.body: `head` is collected from `text.chars().take(limit)`, so it has exactly `limit` characters. The `None` branch appends `…` (one character), producing `limit + 1` characters. The doc comment promises "at most `limit` characters", and the stated use case is a GitHub check-run title cap — exceeding it by one character lets GitHub hard-truncate the title. The tests accept this by asserting `<= 21` (i.e. `limit + 1`) instead of `<= 20`, so they do not catch the off-by-one. Reserving one character for the ellipsis when collecting `head` keeps both branches within `limit`. A degenerate `limit == 0` with non-empty text would still return `"…"`; if that matters to a caller, guard it separately.
findings.title: Keep shorten output within limit when no word boundary is found

value.summary: The new `summarise` module adds character-safe truncation and sentence extraction. The `shorten` function has an off-by-one: when the trimmed head contains no space, the `None` branch returns `limit + 1` characters (head + ellipsis), violating the documented "at most `limit`" contract and potentially exceeding the GitHub title cap it is meant to serve. `first_sentence` is byte-safe because it only matches ASCII ". ".
